title: Recently planted gate — is the rose established enough for full pruning guidance?

common.applies_to: Established or recently planted bush rose; prerequisite check, before the five non-dead-wood pruning observations proceed. Does not restrict dead-wood removal (see §4).
common.preserved_uncertainty: AF-1 as corrected by the Build Check (17 October 2026): rose sources leave a newly planted rose unpruned, apart from dead wood, until it has established, but give no number of years for a bush rose; K-State's Master Gardeners prune at planting and RHS in the first winter (disagreement shown in the restricted reason). AF-2 (Low, not a precaution): the signs of establishment are not used, so an unknown planting date gets the dead-wood-only check.

content.question: Was this rose planted this growing season, so that this is its first season in this spot?

answers.established: No, it has been growing here longer than that
answers.recent: Yes, it was planted this growing season

content.restricted_reason_recent: Most sources leave a newly planted rose unpruned, apart from dead wood, until it has established; two prune at planting or in the first winter. So I'll only look at dead wood today.
content.restricted_reason_fallback: I can't tell whether this rose has established yet, so I'll only look at dead wood today.
